The {{Nihongo|'''Ichinoyama Kofun'''|市ノ山古墳}} is a [[kofun]] located in [[Fujiidera]], [[Osaka]] traditionally believed to be the [[Japanese imperial tombs|burial site]] of [[Emperor Ingyō]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |author=Noboru Sotoike |url=https://iss.ndl.go.jp/books/R100000002-I000007815714-00 |title=Encyclopedia Mausoleum Reference Site: Another Emperor's Mausoleum |publisher=Yoshikawa Kobunkan |year=2005 |isbn=4642013458 |pages=49–52}}</ref>

The kofun is a member of the [[Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Group]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Explanation: the Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group(Part 2)│Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka3d2023/en/explanation_part_02.html |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=野中古墳／大阪大学考古学研究室 |language=ja-JP}}</ref>

[[File:Ichinoyama_Kofun.jpg|thumb|Aerial view]]

== Description ==
The kofun is 230 meters long, with many subsidiary tombs surrounding it. Many of these tombs contained [[Sarcophagus|sarcophagi]] with a "house shaped" design more similar to later designs. This has been interpreted as indicating this kofun was a transitionary period towards later burial practices. This is in line with the decline of the [[keyhole tomb order]] which came after this kofun. With a few exceptions like {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳}}, most kofuns made later than this kofun were smaller compared to this one.<ref name=":1" />

==Association with Emperor Ingyo==
The [[Imperial Household Agency]] designates this location as Ingyō's [[mausoleum]]/''[[kofun]]''-type Imperial tomb. Formally, this tomb is called {{Nihongo|Emperor Ingyō's misasagi|恵我長野北陵,|''Ega no nagano no kita no misasagi''}}.<ref name=":0" />

The actual site of Ingyō's [[Grave (burial)|grave]] is not known, this regent is traditionally venerated at a [[memorial]] [[Shinto]] shrine near the kofun.<ref name="kunaicho">{{cite web |title=允恭天皇 (19) |url=https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/ryobo/guide/019/ |access-date=August 1, 2023 |work=[[Imperial Household Agency]] (Kunaichō) |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author=[[William Gowland|Gowland, William]] |title=The Burial Mounds and Dolmens of the Early Emperors of Japan |publisher=The Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland |year=1907 |volume=37 |pages=10–46}}</ref>  An alternative theory states Ingyo was buried in the nearby {{Nihongo|[[Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]]|津堂城山古墳}}, which is also located in Fujiidera.<ref name=":0" />
